reading: shows: Automattic's Terms say it may offer features that use AI to help set up or operate the website or store, that the merchant answers for Input and Output, and that the AI Guidelines apply (WC-S-0486, WC-S-0853, WC-S-0838). outside: some AI features may be powered by Anthropic and OpenAI, and the input is shared with third-party AI providers, who may train their models on it (WC-S-5347, WC-S-5349), a reading that the providers do the AI's work. No statement places the features in the plugin, its admin or a separate Automattic service, so no core and no own-service: a gap (notes). Joined with the others on role (landings).

core: WooCommerce includes native support for the Model Context Protocol, through which AI assistants and tools interact directly with the store (WC-S-0918), on its own MCP namespace and route (WC-S-5453, WC-S-5454). shows: its feature flag mcp_integration is experimental and off by default (WC-S-5452), not a released flag. core: WooCommerce's own REST API, which connects the store to external systems and services (WC-S-0887), with its namespace wc/v3 and its settings API (WC-S-0078, WC-S-0684), under the settings tab Advanced (WC-S-0011). extension-point: the filter woocommerce_rest_api_get_rest_namespaces (WC-S-0448), Q1's extension point, a reading that extensions add their own namespaces to the API through it. Q1's gaps: who is responsible is stated only in general terms, and no reason was found.

core: WooCommerce's settings section Advanced > REST API keys (WC-S-0023); its REST API has two ways to authenticate (WC-S-0662), and pre-generated keys authenticate the use of its endpoints (WC-S-0921); most integrations need the merchant to generate API keys in WooCommerce and enter them in the external service (WC-S-0888). A reading: the merchant generating keys for an external service is how an app is authorized here; WooCommerce's term is authentication, against Salla's authorization and OAuth (proposed rename, notes).

core: WooCommerce's own access levels Read, Write and Read/Write (WC-S-0277 to WC-S-0279), which Q1 lists as access scopes. That they are a REST API key's permissions is a reading; the statements give only their names. core rests on boundary statements: the platform's own API for its own feature, by the dry run's C1.

searched: protected customer data;personal data;personal information;customer data;PII;sensitive
reading: The concern map holds nothing found for the platform approving or bounding an app's access to buyers' personal data. The hits are other things: Marketplace developers get no customers' personal information about their sales (WC-S-5340, cited in CM-APP-002), the Store API holds no sensitive data (WC-C-079, domain E), Jetpack's JSON API (WC-C-117) and the store's privacy erasers (WC-C-045, domain A).

terms: Rate Limiting for Store API endpoints
reading: core: rate limiting is available for the Store API's endpoints, optional and off by default (WC-S-5358). shows: its reason, to prevent abuse from excessive calls and performance degradation (WC-S-5363). A reading: these are limits on requests to the platform's own Store API, the public storefront API, not on an app's calls to the REST API; no statement of a REST API limit is held. WC-C-031 is domain A's, which names F under also; its checkout setting (WC-S-0932) is left to A, as the anchor kept Shopify's bot protection apart (U-045).

core: WooCommerce's REST API has the versioned namespaces wc/v1, wc/v2, wc/v3 and wc/v4 (WC-S-0076 to WC-S-0080), and the settings section Advanced > Legacy API (WC-S-0026). A reading: the namespaces are the API's versions; no statement says when a version is added or retired, and no change log is held (notes).

core: WooCommerce's webhooks API creates, views, updates and deletes individual webhooks or a batch of them (WC-S-0683). A reading, for the reviewer: a batch request is one form of an operation in bulk; nothing held shows it asynchronous, or a topic when it finishes, as Shopify's are. The same batch is stated for products, orders, customers and coupons (WC-C-064, WC-C-070, WC-C-073, WC-C-074), of other domains, left uncited.

Q1's gap: who is responsible is stated only in general terms.
core: WooCommerce's settings section Advanced > Webhooks (WC-S-0025), from which, a reading, the merchant sends the store's events to a URL of its choice (WC-S-0885), without an app.

core: WooCommerce's admin menu WooCommerce > Extensions (WC-S-0046) and its onboarding task Enhance your store with extensions (WC-S-0421). extension-point: extensions and plugins provided or manufactured by a third party, which the merchant may enable, use or purchase (WC-S-0852), and Marketplace developers who create, maintain and support their own products (WC-S-5342). shows: Automattic doesn't vet, endorse or control Third-Party Services, which are used at the merchant's own risk (WC-S-0487, WC-S-0656), though the plugin's readme says its developers vet each new extension (WC-S-0596, CM-APP-002); extensions may have their own requirements and terms (WC-S-0465); their software is under the GPL (WC-S-0645); developers must make them comply with GDPR (WC-S-5343, scope EU). Q1's gap: no reason found.

core: WooCommerce's own Marketplace rules: it may suspend or remove a Product (WC-S-0583), its developers vet each new extension (WC-S-0596), a listed Product must be GPL compatible (WC-S-0577), each product shows its developer (WC-S-5341); and the admin's onboarding task touring the Marketplace (WC-S-0432). extension-point: the Marketplace connects developers and merchants (WC-S-0923), with its category Extensions (WC-S-0694). shows: Marketplace developers see aggregate sales data, no customers' personal information (WC-S-5340), and User Data is WooCommerce's Confidential Information (WC-S-0584). A reading: the Marketplace is WooCommerce's own, run by WooCommerce, Inc. (WC-S-0576), and reached from the admin, so core, not own-service (notes). Its category Themes (WC-S-0695) is left to domain E (U-051).

core: WooCommerce collects the revenue of a Marketplace purchase and pays the Partner 70% of it (WC-S-0580), a reading that it keeps the rest; a purchase gives a WooCommerce.com subscription (WC-S-0900), which the merchant manages from the admin (WC-S-0899); WooCommerce refunds a purchase in full within 30 days and handles refund and cancellation claims, while the Partner answers for taxes (WC-S-0834, WC-S-0581). The same 70% clause, under its responsible key, is cited in CM-PTN-003 (notes).
